title: Self-equivalent permutation representatives of APN CCZ classes
summary: Determine whether every APN permutation is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation with a nontrivial linear-equivalence automorphism.

formal_statement.body: For every APN permutation $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$, does there exist a permutation $G$ CCZ-equivalent to $F$ such that $$|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LE}}(G)|>1?$$ Prove existence for every APN permutation, or find a CCZ class in which every permutation representative has trivial linear-equivalence automorphism group.

scope.domain: Permutation representatives and linear-equivalence automorphisms in APN CCZ classes
assumptions: $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$ is an APN permutation
$G$ must be both a permutation and CCZ-equivalent to $F$
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove the representative exists in every APN-permutation CCZ class, or exhibit a class whose permutation representatives all have trivial Aut_LE.

citations.label: Beierle--Brinkmann--Leander, APN-permutation representative conjecture
citations.locator: Conjecture 1 and Conclusion, journal pp. 4868 and 4874

progress.summary: The second clause of Conjecture 1 asks for a permutation representative with nontrivial linear-equivalence automorphism in every APN-permutation CCZ class.
